chunks: I bought a slave girl in Basra from a woman, and she informed me that no one had had intercourse with her. So I had intercourse with her, and I did not observe her waiting period (istibra'). I asked about that Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and he said, 'That is so; I have done that, and I do not intend to return (to not doing it).'

And whenever a man frees his slave girl, it is permissible for him to contract marriage with her before the istibra', and this is not permissible for others, until he observes her istibra' by three months or three menstrual periods.

key_terms.اِسْتِبْرَاء: istibra' (waiting period to check for pregnancy)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (istibra') for a freed slave girl who was a virgin when purchased?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) validates the practice of istibra' by citing his own personal experience, thereby establishing a strong precedent for the ruling. The hadith clarifies a specific legal nuance: while a master who purchases a virgin slave-girl may marry her immediately upon manumission without waiting for the istibra' period, other men must observe the full waiting period of three months or three menstrual cycles to ensure lineage purity.
